value.text: Erb palsy results from injury to the {{c1::upper trunk (C5-C6)}} of the brachial plexus, presenting with the classic {{c2::waiter's tip}} deformity (adducted, internally rotated arm and pronated forearm).
value.subject: Anatomy

value.text: Klumpke palsy results from injury to the {{c1::lower trunk (C8-T1)}} of the brachial plexus, leading to {{c2::claw hand}} due to intrinsic hand muscle paralysis and concomitant {{c3::Horner syndrome}} if sympathetic fibers are involved.
value.subject: Anatomy

value.front: Which structure passes through the foramen spinosum and what is its clinical significance?
value.back:
Middle Meningeal Artery (branch of maxillary artery).
Laceration by pterion fracture leads to an Epidural Hematoma (biconvex/lenticular shape on CT) with a classic lucid interval.
value.subject: Anatomy

value.front: What are the boundaries and contents of the Femoral Ring?
value.back:
Boundaries:
• Anterior: Inguinal ligament
• Medial: Lacunar ligament (Gimbernat)
• Lateral: Femoral vein septum
• Posterior: Pectineal ligament (Cooper)
Content: Cloquet lymph node / fat. Site of Femoral Hernia.
value.subject: Anatomy

value.text: The {{c1::Abducens nerve (CN VI)}} is the only cranial nerve that runs freely inside the cavernous sinus next to the {{c2::internal carotid artery}}, making it the earliest nerve affected in cavernous sinus thrombosis or ICA aneurysm.
value.subject: Anatomy

value.front: What are the derivatives of the 3rd and 4th Pharyngeal Pouches?
value.back:
• 3rd Pouch: Inferior parathyroid glands + Thymus (mnemonic: 3 letters in SIT)
• 4th Pouch: Superior parathyroid glands + Ultimobranchial body (Parafollicular C-cells of thyroid).
value.subject: Anatomy

value.text: Phase 0 of the ventricular cardiac action potential is caused by rapid {{c1::Na+ influx via fast voltage-gated Na+ channels}}, while Phase 2 (plateau) is sustained by {{c2::Ca2+ influx via L-type calcium channels}} balancing K+ efflux.
value.subject: Physiology

value.front: How does Inulin clearance differ from PAH clearance in renal physiology?
value.back:
• Inulin: Freely filtered, neither reabsorbed nor secreted -> used to calculate Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR).
• PAH (Para-aminohippuric acid): Freely filtered and actively secreted -> used to calculate Effective Renal Plasma Flow (eRPF).
value.subject: Physiology

value.text: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is caused by a deficiency of {{c1::Phenylalanine Hydroxylase (PAH)}} or its cofactor {{c2::Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4)}}, leading to musty/mousy body odor and elevated phenylketones.
value.subject: Biochemistry

value.front: What is the biochemical hallmark and clinical manifestation of Wernicke-Korsakoff Syndrome?
value.back:
Deficiency of Thiamine (Vitamin B1), which impairs pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.
Classic Triad: Encephalopathy + Oculomotor dysfunction (nystagmus, ophthalmoplegia) + Ataxia. Korsakoff adds confabulation and anterograde amnesia (mammillary body necrosis).
value.subject: Biochemistry

value.text: The drug of choice for acute organophosphate poisoning is {{c1::Atropine}} (competitive muscarinic antagonist to reverse SLUDGE symptoms) combined with {{c2::Pralidoxime (2-PAM)}} to reactivate phosphorylated acetylcholinesterase before aging occurs.
value.subject: Pharmacology

value.front: Why are ACE Inhibitors (e.g. Enalapril) contraindicated in Bilateral Renal Artery Stenosis?
value.back: ACE inhibitors inhibit Angiotensin II-mediated constriction of the efferent arteriole. In bilateral renal artery stenosis, GFR is highly dependent on efferent vasoconstriction; blocking this causes a precipitous drop in intraglomerular pressure and acute renal failure.
value.subject: Pharmacology

value.text: {{c1::Adenosine}} is the drug of choice for terminating Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia (PSVT), acting on {{c2::A1 receptors}} to activate potassium channels and hyperpolarize the AV node. Its ultra-short half-life is < {{c3::10 seconds}}.
value.subject: Pharmacology

value.front: Classify First-Line Anti-Tubercular Drugs (HRZE) with their hallmark adverse effects:
value.back:
• Isoniazid (H): Peripheral neuropathy (prevent with Pyridoxine/Vit B6), Hepatotoxicity, Sideroblastic anemia
  • Rifampicin (R): Orange/red urine & secretions, CYP450 inducer, Hepatotoxicity
  • Pyrazinamide (Z): Hyperuricemia (Gout), Hepatotoxicity (most hepatotoxic)
  • Ethambutol (E): Optic neuritis (red-green color blindness), hyperuricemia
value.subject: Pharmacology

value.text: {{c1::Sugammadex}} is a modified gamma-cyclodextrin that selectively binds and encapsulates {{c2::Rocuronium and Vecuronium}}, providing rapid reversal of neuromuscular blockade without cholinergic side effects.
value.subject: Pharmacology

value.text: In Burkitt Lymphoma, the characteristic cytogenetic translocation is {{c1::t(8;14)}}, causing overexpression of the {{c2::c-MYC}} oncogene, producing a pathognomonic {{c3::starry sky appearance}} on histology.
value.subject: Pathology

value.front: Contrast the histopathologic findings of Crohn Disease vs Ulcerative Colitis:
value.back:
FeatureCrohn DiseaseUlcerative Colitis
LocationAnywhere (terminal ileum most common), Skip lesionsRectum extending proximally, continuous
DepthTransmural (fistulae, creeping fat)Mucosa and submucosa only
GranulomasNon-caseating granulomas (50%)Crypt abscesses, NO granulomas
Lead-pipe signCobblestone mucosa, string sign of KantorLead-pipe colon on barium
value.subject: Pathology

value.text: {{c1::Reed-Sternberg cells}} (binucleated "owl-eye" appearance with prominent eosinophilic nucleoli) are diagnostic of {{c2::Hodgkin Lymphoma}} and typically express surface markers {{c3::CD15 and CD30}}.
value.subject: Pathology

value.front: What is the characteristic histological finding in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma?
value.back:
• Orphan Annie eye nuclei (ground-glass empty-appearing nuclei)
• Nuclear pseudo-inclusions and grooves ("coffee bean" nuclei)
• Psammoma bodies (concentric lamellated calcifications).
value.subject: Pathology

value.front: Interpret the Serological Markers of Hepatitis B Virus Infection:
value.back:
• HBsAg (+): Active infection (acute or chronic if > 6 months)
  • Anti-HBs (+): Immunity (via vaccination if isolated, or recovery if Anti-HBc IgG also +)
  • Anti-HBc IgM (+): Acute / recent infection (sole marker in "Window Period")
  • HBeAg (+): High viral replication, high infectivity
  • Anti-HBe (+): Low viral replication, low infectivity
value.subject: Microbiology

value.text: The causative organism of Syphilis is {{c1::Treponema pallidum}} (spirochete), best visualized using {{c2::Dark-field microscopy}} in primary chancre. Screening is done with {{c3::VDRL / RPR}} and confirmed via {{c4::FTA-ABS / TPHA}}.
value.subject: Microbiology

value.text: {{c1::Streptococcus pneumoniae}} is catalase negative, alpha-hemolytic, {{c2::optochin sensitive}}, and {{c3::bile soluble}}, with a polysaccharide capsule producing a positive Neufeld Quellung reaction.
value.subject: Microbiology

value.text: {{c1::Chipping (powder tattooing)}} around a firearm entry wound occurs in {{c2::close range (up to 1-2 feet)}} firing, caused by unburnt gunpowder particles embedded into the dermis.
value.subject: Forensic Medicine

value.front: What is Casper Dictum regarding the rate of postmortem putrefaction?
value.back: Rate of putrefaction: 1 week in Air = 2 weeks in Water = 8 weeks in Earth (Buried) (Ratio 1 : 2 : 8).
value.subject: Forensic Medicine

value.text: The epidemiological study design that is best suited for rare diseases is the {{c1::Case-Control study}} (measure of association: {{c2::Odds Ratio}}), whereas the {{c3::Cohort study}} is best for rare exposures (measure: {{c4::Relative Risk}}).
value.subject: Social and Preventive Medicine

value.front: Define Sensitivity, Specificity, Positive Predictive Value (PPV) and Negative Predictive Value (NPV):
value.back:
• Sensitivity: TP / (TP + FN) — true positive rate, rules OUT disease (SnOUT)
• Specificity: TN / (TN + FP) — true negative rate, rules IN disease (SpIN)
• PPV: TP / (TP + FP) — directly proportional to disease prevalence
• NPV: TN / (TN + FN) — inversely proportional to disease prevalence.
value.subject: Social and Preventive Medicine

value.front: Differentiate Rinne and Weber Tuning Fork Tests in Conductive vs Sensorineural Hearing Loss:
value.back:
• Rinne Test (512 Hz):
    • Normal / SNHL: Air Conduction > Bone Conduction (Positive)
    • Conductive Hearing Loss: Bone Conduction > Air Conduction (Negative)
  • Weber Test:
    • Conductive Loss: Lateralizes to the affected (bad) ear
    • Sensorineural Loss: Lateralizes to the unaffected (normal/better) ear
value.subject: ENT

value.text: Meniere disease is caused by {{c1::endolymphatic hydrops}} and is characterized by the classic tetrad of: {{c2::episodic rotational vertigo}}, {{c3::fluctuating low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss}}, {{c4::tinnitus}}, and {{c5::aural fullness}}.
value.subject: ENT

value.front: What is Trotter Triad in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma?
value.back:
1. Conductive deafness (due to Eustachian tube obstruction)
2. Ipsilateral facial pain / numbness (involving CN V3)
3. Palatal paralysis (involving CN X)
value.subject: ENT

value.text: In Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma, the definitive surgical treatment of choice is {{c1::Laser Peripheral Iridotomy (LPI)}} in both the affected and fellow prophylactic eye.
value.subject: Ophthalmology

value.front: What are the classic fundus findings of Central Retinal Artery Occlusion (CRAO)?
value.back:
• Cherry-red spot at the fovea (due to choroidal circulation shining through thin foveal retina)
• Diffuse retinal pallor / milky white edema
• Boxcarring (cattle-trucking) of retinal vessels
• Sudden, painless, severe monocular vision loss.
value.subject: Ophthalmology

value.text: In ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI), ST elevations in leads V1-V4 indicate an {{c1::Anterior wall}} infarction supplied by the {{c2::Left Anterior Descending (LAD)}} artery.
value.subject: General Medicine

value.front: What is the diagnostic criteria and treatment of choice for Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)?
value.back:
Triad: Hyperglycemia (> 250 mg/dL), High Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis (pH < 7.3, HCO3 < 18), Ketonemia / Ketonuria.
Management:
1. IV 0.9% Normal Saline hydration (most crucial initial step)
2. Regular IV Insulin infusion (0.1 U/kg/hr) — check Potassium FIRST (do not start if K+ < 3.3)
3. Potassium replacement to prevent hypokalemia.
value.subject: General Medicine

value.text: In trauma evaluation, the FAST exam (Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma) evaluates 4 acoustic windows: {{c1::Morison pouch (hepatorenal)}}, {{c2::splenorenal recess}}, {{c3::suprapubic (pouch of Douglas)}}, and {{c4::subxiphoid pericardial window}}.
value.subject: General Surgery

value.front: What is the most common cause of early vs late Post-Thyroidectomy Hemorrhage?
value.back:
• Reactionary Hemorrhage (first 24 hours): Slipped ligature on superior thyroid artery; causes rapid tracheal compression & airway compromise. Immediate bedside wound reopening is mandatory!
• Secondary Hemorrhage (7-10 days): Wound infection eroding a vessel.
value.subject: General Surgery

value.text: The drug of choice for the prevention and treatment of seizures in severe preeclampsia and eclampsia is {{c1::Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4)}} using the {{c2::Pritchard regimen}} (loading + maintenance). Toxicity is monitored via {{c3::patellar tendon reflex}}, respiratory rate (> 12/min), and urine output (> 30 mL/hr). Antidote is {{c4::Calcium Gluconate}}.
value.subject: Obstetrics and Gynecology

value.front: What is the single most common cyanotic congenital heart disease manifesting in the neonatal period vs infancy?
value.back:
• Neonatal Period (Day 1-2): Transposition of Great Arteries (TGA) - "Egg on string" appearance on X-ray.
• After 1 Month / Infancy: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) - "Boot-shaped heart" on X-ray, presenting with cyanotic "tet spells".
value.subject: Pediatrics

value.text: {{c1::Auspitz sign}} (pinpoint bleeding upon scraping silvery scales) and {{c2::Koebner phenomenon}} (isomorphic response at sites of trauma) are classic clinical features of {{c3::Psoriasis vulgaris}}.
value.subject: Dermatology

value.front: Differentiate Pemphigus Vulgaris vs Bullous Pemphigoid on Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF):
value.back:
• Pemphigus Vulgaris: Antibodies against Desmoglein 3/1; Intraepidermal flaccid bullae, Nikolsky (+); DIF shows intercellular fishnet/lace-like IgG/C3 pattern.
• Bullous Pemphigoid: Antibodies against Hemidesmosomes (BP180/BP230); Subepidermal tense bullae, Nikolsky (-); DIF shows linear basement membrane IgG/C3 band.
value.subject: Dermatology

value.text: The first-line mood stabilizer for classic acute mania and bipolar maintenance is {{c1::Lithium}} (therapeutic range: {{c2::0.6 - 1.2 mEq/L}}). Toxicity requires hemodialysis if levels exceed {{c3::4.0 mEq/L}} or severe neurotoxicity.
value.subject: Psychiatry

value.front: Identify the classic radiographic signs associated with these chest conditions:
value.back:
• Hampton Hump: Wedge-shaped peripheral opacity pointing to hilum -> Pulmonary Embolism / Infarct.
• Westermark Sign: Focal oligemia distal to occluded vessel -> Pulmonary Embolism.
• Gloved Finger Sign: Bronchial impaction -> Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis (ABPA).
• Continuous Diaphragm Sign: Pneumomediastinum.

value.text: A fracture of the proximal third of the ulna with dislocation of the radial head is known as {{c1::Monteggia fracture-dislocation}} (nerve injured: {{c2::Posterior Interosseous Nerve / PIN}}), whereas a fracture of distal third of radius with DRUJ dislocation is {{c3::Galeazzi fracture}}.
